_comment: Round 2 of the de-ossification port: twenty more Vector3 methods and three more Matrix44
methods, all in code/midtown2/vector7/vector3.cpp and matrix44.cpp.
THIS FILE MUST BE MERGED INTO data/ported.json BEFORE THE NEXT BUILD. tools/asm.py reads only
data/ported.json, and it stops the build when a header says ARTS_EXPORT for a symbol that file
does not list - the dangerous direction, an export with no C++ behind it. The headers here have
already been flipped, so the two are out of step until the merge happens.
tools/genheaders.py also reads only data/ported.json. Running it before the merge regenerates
vector3.h and matrix44.h with these back as ARTS_IMPORT and silently undoes the flips.
Every symbol below was read off the disassembly of its own bytes - capstone over the PROC in
game.asm.pristine, cross-checked against midtown2.exe at the map's RVA - and every one was
checked with tools/verify_arity.py first. All twenty-three are among the 6,315 symbols whose
terminating `ret imm16` agrees with the parameter list their mangled name encodes.
DELIBERATELY NOT HERE:
?InvScale@Vector3@@QAEXM@Z            0x595B70. A seventh Trap 14 symbol, and one
verify_arity.py cannot see: the arity agrees (`ret 4`)
but the argument is dereferenced at +0/+4/+8, so it is a
pointer, and the body is a dot product left in st(0).
The code is ?Dot@Vector3@@QBEMABV1@@Z, not an InvScale.
?Dot3x3Transpose@Vector3@@QAEXABVMatrix34@@@Z
0x4795C0. The map gives it 2,320 bytes against 96 for
its sibling Dot3x3 - Trap 7. Its real extent has to be
settled before the body can be read.
?InvertTo@Matrix44@@QBEXAAV1@@Z       0x4C1510, 1,766 bytes. Not Gauss-Jordan with pivoting:
it calls Determinant, takes 1.0f/det, and expands
sixteen straight-line cofactors. No loop, no pivot, no
row swap. Mechanical but 288 member reads with nothing
to cross-check them against; it gets its own pass.
the six Trap 14 Vector3 symbols       Add, AddScaled, Subtract, SubtractScaled,
Scale(const Vector3&, f32) and operator*=. Permanent.
